cover: Prompt injection: audit your AI feature

slides.title: What does it read?
slides.body: Emails, web pages, PDFs, CVs, calendar invites, reviews. Anything someone outside can write can carry instructions.

slides.title: What private data can it see?
slides.body: It should only pull up what the person asking is allowed to see, checked in code each time they ask.

slides.title: Can it send anything out?
slides.body: Email, a web request, even a link it renders. Outside content plus private data plus a way out is the risky mix.

slides.title: What can it do without a person?
slides.body: Refunds, deletions, payments and customer messages should wait for approval. An assistant that drafts replies doesn't need to send them.

slides.title: Is its output checked?
slides.body: If it should be a category from a fixed list, reject anything else. If it should never contain a link, strip links.

slides.title: Have you attacked it yourself?
slides.body: Hidden instructions in documents, hijacking emails, requests to reveal its own instructions. Then log what it does after launch.
